claim: For either of the two opposite 13-point minimal finite models \(P\) of \(\mathbb{RP}^2\), a continuous self-map \(f:P\to P\) induces a nonzero map on \(H_1(P;\mathbf F_2)\) if and only if \(f\) is a homeomorphism. Exactly 24 self-maps have nonzero action, forming \(\operatorname{Aut}(P)\cong S_4\); an exhaustive certificate enumerates 562333 continuous self-maps in total.

correctness.rationale: The explicit poset and order complex are reconstructed from scratch. The verifier proves mod-2 H1 has dimension one, exhaustively enumerates all isotone self-maps, and tests each induced action using a computed cocycle paired with a generating cycle. Exactly 24 of 562333 maps act nontrivially; all 24 are bijections and their inverses are verified isotone. Conversely every homeomorphism induces the nonzero automorphism of one-dimensional H1.

evidence: Barmak's general theorem that a self-map of a minimal finite space homotopic to the identity is the identity has a much stronger hypothesis and does not imply the claim.
Cianci--Ottina classify the minimal models but not their endomorphism monoids.
Classical RP2 homology does not by itself force a self-map to be a homeomorphism.

value.rationale: The principal claim is a structural rigidity result, not an arbitrary table entry: on the smallest finite RP2 models, preserving the unique mod-2 H1 class already forces a homeomorphism. It identifies a sharp representational boundary and supplies a reproducible benchmark for finite-space map algorithms.
